artifact: Cascadia Early Warning, revision of charts 1 and 4

findings.quote: The label says "point 736 is the tick", but I couldn't find a tick among the dots on the desktop version.
findings.note: the tick runs past the widest row of dots on both sides

findings.quote: they say the three-month ranges held 20 of 22 test months, but the band they drew is the one-month band, so I never saw the test the headline is selling.
findings.note: the title states only what the picture carries; the coverage is the subtitle's basis and a second table lists the 22 months

findings.quote: The September 2026 estimate (672, 329 to 838) is described in the text, but I couldn't find it on the chart.
findings.note: September leaves the chart's subtitle and strip; it stays beside the card and in the table, undrawn

findings.quote: The phone also has a thin vertical line labelled "80% range" sitting right by the "May '24" tick. On first glance it looked like an event marker, or like the band starts in May 2024.
findings.note: the narrow label names its month: 80% range from Jan '24

findings.quote: the firm-list exclusion of 1 of 649,080 reports. DSQ alone can't be 649,080 reports, so I don't know what population that number refers to.
findings.note: the strip says across the seven codes; the subtitle says after the firm-list exclusion, not eligible

findings.quote: I also didn't follow some of the wording: "eligible" reports (eligible for what?), "ETS candidate", "locked-test months"
findings.note: eligible is replaced and locked-test leaves the title; ETS candidate is the model's name and the method section explains it

findings.quote: The main chart on the phone is cramped: three date labels, "exp."/"rec." as labels, and I couldn't tell where the green line leaves the band.
findings.note: 56 months in 280 CSS px; stacking grew the plot from 110 to 158 px; table and navigator carry the values

findings.quote: the phone's dots sit in about the first fifth of a 0–3K axis, which makes them tiny and uncountable.
findings.note: the strip shares the history's value scale so it reads against it

findings.quote: the November dots are a vertical column next to the series with no axis of their own. I assumed they share the left axis, but nothing says so
findings.note: the column is labelled with its month and horizon; empty September and October slots would draw a gap as data

findings.quote: the 20 dots are tightly packed. I could not get a confident count, or a clean filled/hollow split, at desktop size.
findings.note: the count is in the subtitle and summary; the dots carry the spread

findings.quote: the end labels ("Jan '22", "Aug '26") seem to be aligned to their outer edges rather than centred. Their midpoints therefore sit a few months inside the dates they mark.
findings.note: declared narrow rule (first panel F-5): edge labels pulled inside the plot so they are not clipped; also chart 4

findings.quote: in 2024–26 the dashed blue and green lines cross constantly, and the dashed line is often hidden.
findings.note: received is drawn on top by design; the table carries both

findings.quote: There's no split for deaths, injuries and malfunctions, none for initial versus supplemental reports
findings.note: the module publishes counts by design; the strip says counts, not rates

findings.quote: It's 91%, which tells me the range is wider than it claims, or there are too few months to say.
findings.note: a correct reading, not a misreading; chart 3 reports above-nominal coverage as a calibration finding

findings.quote: It's called the ETS "candidate", so what was it up against, and was it picked using the same 22 locked-test months it's now being scored on?
findings.note: a question chart 2's subtitle and the chronology answer: selection used targets through 2023-12

findings.quote: are that 2022 spike and the drop since then mostly one manufacturer's filing behaviour?
findings.note: the module names no firm and attributes no count, by decision

findings.quote: I didn't understand what "coverage" means in "where coverage enabled it."
findings.note: title, subtitle, H2 and KPI use the lanes' own words: where the rule is on, if it ran in every code

findings.quote: The red note about the one episode moves below the chart, away from the DSP lane, so I had to hunt for which mark it meant
findings.note: at the narrow width a short label stands at the episode in reserved headroom

findings.quote: On the phone the shapes run together. The OZD lane in particular is a string of squares and diamonds I couldn't separate or count
findings.note: 32 months by 7 lanes in 280 CSS px (first panel finding 18); diamonds raised further

findings.quote: The seven ungated episodes aren't drawn as bars in the "rule off" lanes, so I'd have to pair up the hollow squares myself.
findings.note: outlined bars in rule-off lanes: one filled and six outlined are the title's seven

findings.quote: Diamonds collide with squares. The "raised" offset is smaller than the glyph, so they merge
findings.note: diamonds raised to -14 px (-11 narrow) and same-month diamonds stepped 12 px (9 narrow)

findings.quote: I looked for what "preceded" means, meaning what lead time counts.
findings.note: the subtitle: preceded by the start of a queue episode within the eighteen months before

findings.quote: "1,751 arrived against 678 expected" ... It reads like two months added together against two months expected, but it doesn't say so
findings.note: the annotation says peak month

findings.quote: The codes have no names except DSQ, which I only know from the first chart.
findings.note: seven device names do not fit lane labels (first panel finding 4); tooltip and table carry them

findings.quote: The phone subtitle is also a full screen of text before you reach the chart.
findings.note: the subtitle carries the mark key and the gate's basis, which must travel with the chart (4.3)

findings.quote: "128 code-months" / "all 224": Not drawn. You can only rebuild them from structure
findings.note: the counts leave the title for the subtitle

findings.quote: If you freeze the gate at the end of 2025 and score only Jan to Aug 2026, the months it never saw, what does the rule do?
findings.note: a chronological test of the queue, out of scope by Aaron's decision (D19); the subtitle names the locked span

findings.quote: If Class I is the only yardstick, "zero of 24" tells me less than it sounds like it does.
findings.note: the one pre-registered count; association only, as the subtitle says

findings.quote: A one-sided 80% bound should be beaten about one month in ten, so roughly 22 of 224, and 30 isn't far off that.
findings.note: a correct reading; the chance illustration is in the method section

findings.quote: No divider between the rule-on and rule-off groups.
findings.note: a preference: the lane labels say rule off and the marks are hollow

findings.quote: The one risk is the pale highlight around the gated episode. In grey it nearly matches the background
findings.note: the filled bar carries an outline

findings.quote: "Rule off" is shortened to "off", so "PYX off" read to me like the code was discontinued.
findings.note: declared narrow abbreviation (first panel finding 17)

findings.quote: I also can't tell from the title whether one episode is the rule working or failing.
findings.note: interpretation; the page says an empty queue is a valid result

findings.quote: what anyone did with the one DSP episode: was it looked into, and was a cause found
findings.note: dispositions are the reader's act; the case study's next test describes it

findings.quote: there's no sense of how many reports one episode would put in front of my team.
findings.note: the queue's unit is the episode, by the registered rule
